observations: A start refused before it applies (a blank --selected-by, or an input the workflow refuses) writes its refused row to the item's own file and marks its source seen. A corrected start from the same session is then a duplicate, and one from another session is not-owner, so the item id can never start. This was already true on main for a bad input; the new selection check adds one more way in. It belongs in a plan item.
The real run's rows say release 0.1.0: bin/host.js was run from the checkout with no --release, so it read the repo's plugin.json (0.1.0), not the installed 0.1.42.

The final child started at 10:07:30Z, as soon as the last slice ended, before this verdict, though the item's text expected it to start after. finishing has no hold, so the order the item planned isn't something the builder can choose. Nothing broke: the final child's builder pushed one commit, 46c5a010 (sessionKey reads any URL ending in the id), and returned the PR. I verified at that head.

sessionKey now strips any scheme://.../ prefix, so a URL from another host that ends in session_X keys the same as the Claude session. That's harmless for trailers and capture rows, but broader than the forms the item names.
time's ci label reads only UserPromptSubmit wakes. A GitHub event read through ReadNotifications makes no wake row, so it can't be counted as CI waiting.
